nodes.label: ENC(<id>:<ciphertext>) self-describing envelope
nodes.rationale: ENC( is a reserved marker no plaintext JSON value can start with. Recording the cipher id in the row gives three properties: self-describing reads (decryptor chosen from the row, not config), mixed plaintext/b64/aesgcm stores that all read back correctly (foundation for rotation), and safe toggling since enabling/disabling changes only new writes.

nodes.label: EncryptingSerializer
nodes.rationale: Encryption is a decorator over the Serializer — the single boundary where a payload becomes a persisted string — so it transforms only the PAYLOAD column and leaves the rest of the failover flow untouched. Scoped to JDBC because only that store persists a string.

nodes.label: PayloadCipher SPI
nodes.rationale: Ciphers deal in raw ciphertext only; the EncryptingSerializer owns the envelope so implementors never parse it. id() must be unique and contain neither ':' nor ')' because it is persisted in every row — changing it strands existing rows.

nodes.label: Cipher registry (read) + active write cipher
nodes.rationale: All PayloadCipher beans are indexed by id() for reads while exactly one, chosen by failover.store.jdbc.encryption.cipher, is the active write cipher. An unknown id on read raises FailoverStoreException rather than returning garbage.

nodes.label: Base64PayloadCipher (id b64)
nodes.rationale: Zero-dependency default and worked example of the SPI, providing no confidentiality — a loud WARN fires when it is the active write cipher. It is given a cipher id specifically so mismatches fail loudly: a bare Base64 decoder would happily 'decode' AES ciphertext into garbage and surface a confusing JSON error three layers away.

nodes.label: Encryption vs. deserialization allowlist orthogonality
nodes.rationale: PAYLOAD (data) is encrypted but PAYLOAD_CLASS (type name) is not, so on read the payload is decrypted first and the allowlist still gates class loading on the real plaintext class name. Encryption hides data; the allowlist constrains which classes may be instantiated.

nodes.label: What payload encryption is not
nodes.rationale: Not transport security, not a substitute for DB/disk encryption or access control (defense in depth only), not key management (your PayloadCipher owns the keys), and not available for non-JDBC stores.

edges.source_location: both obscure business data at rest via a deterministic reversible-or-hashed transform
